page: The UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-1xCPU-8GB is a virtual server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features a single shared vCPU from an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is configured with 8.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a high 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. This server operates on the x86_64 architecture, does not include local storage, and lacks dedicated GPU hardware. One complimentary public IPv4 address is bundled with the instance.

Performance benchmarks reveal a highly polarized capability profile. The server achieves a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2228.0, placing it in the top 10% for single-threaded burst tasks. However, due to its shared single-core configuration, multi-core and sustained workloads perform poorly. The Geekbench multi-core score is 2065.0, and the Passmark CPU score is 2006.22, both falling into the lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth at 16.01 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 13.83 GB/sec.

This resource allocation offers a cost-efficient entry point for lightweight, memory-leaning workloads that do not require sustained CPU performance. It is well-suited for basic text processing, single-threaded compression tasks, and simple utility scripts. It is not recommended for database operations, multi-threaded software compilation, or high-throughput web serving, as these workloads are limited by the shared CPU allocation and low memory bandwidth.
